subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB370 LANDED (w1091e): CONFORMS. Both halves re-measured and now pinned by the spec-derived conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/pb370_read_relative_invalid_key: a random READ of RRN 4 takes NOT INVALID KEY with REC-4 and the next READ NEXT gives RRN 5; a random READ of RRN 2 then READ NEXT gives RRN 4, not 6 - the file position indicator is the RELATIVE KEY value, not a cursor; RRN 3 (never written), 9 (past the end) and 0 take INVALID KEY with '23' (§9.1.13.5 3) a), 'randomly access a record that does not exist'); with no INVALID KEY phrase (RRN 7) §9.1.14 3) runs the file's USE procedure. The refuter's editions objection (Annex E.2 item 19 a) as a 2023-only declarative tier) is the one kb/Work PB344 adjudicated on the sibling GR28: §9.1.14 is edition-invariant, Annex E being informative and scoped to one prior edition (cite.py --check E.1 OK), so 1985/2002/2014/2023 stands. || kb/Work PB370. Rule text validated (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "sets the file position indicator to the value contained in the data item referenced by the RELATIVE KEY clause" => OK 29)). Both halves verified. Success: KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead emits `FileSetRelativeKey(name, (long)<typed RELATIVE KEY field>)` before the read (the RRN travels through the typed field, never a byte decode), RelativeConnector.SetPendingKey stages it, and ReadRandom does `_slots.TryGetValue(_pendingKey, …)` then `_fpi = _pendingKey; _lastSlot = _pendingKey;` and makes the slot's image available — 'the record whose relative record number equals the file position indicator is made available'. Failure: no such slot (including RRN 0 or negative, which the 1-based SortedDictionary cannot hold) returns '23' and sets LastReadUnsuccessful, and the emitter routes '2x' to the INVALID KEY imperative per §9.1.14, so 'the invalid key condition exists and execution … is unsuccessful' holds. The FPI is not written on the failing path; that is not observable, because LastReadUnsuccessful already makes the next sequential READ '46' (GR21 first paragraph) and REWRITE/DELETE address `_pendingKey`, not `_fpi`. Partial spec-derived coverage of the SUCCESS leg only: conformance:cases/9.1.13.9-File-sharing-conflict-condition-with-unsuccessful/file_sharing ('IGN=ALPHA' — a Format-2 relative READ delivering the record at the staged RRN); the invalid-key leg is covered only by the legacy-baked KeyedIoDifferentialTests, so test-ref is left empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Same defect as GR28, and I measured it on GR29's OWN trigger rather than carrying it across: a Format-2 relative READ naming an RRN that does not exist in a PRESENT physical file. GR29's second sentence is 'the invalid key condition exists and execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful. (See 9.1.14, Invalid key condition.)', so the §9.1.14 routing is part of what the rule requires, and Annex E.2 item 19 a) makes the open-mode declarative tier on that condition a 2023 behaviour. WiseOwl COBOL runs it under --std 85/2002/2014 as well, so the record's '1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023' overclaims by three editions. Everything else in the rule is right, and I verified more of it than the adjudication did: the note calls the FPI half unobservable on the failing path, but the SUCCESS half's FPI is directly observable and I observed it - a random read of RRN 2 followed by READ NEXT correctly yields RRN 4 (RRN 3 deleted), and RRN 4 then yields RRN 5, so the FPI really is set from the RELATIVE KEY value and not merely from a last-slot cursor. The invalid-key leg is right on all three shapes that can miss (a deleted slot, RRN 0 which the 1-based store cannot hold, and an out-of-range RRN), and on COMP and PACKED-DECIMAL relative keys. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023
